//: THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO `update` HOOK ON Write|Edit ANY MORE.
This file used to carry `code-review-graph update --skip-flows` on a Write|Edit|Bash
matcher with a 30 s timeout. Measured on a 2,679-file repo with an embedding index, that
command takes 90-200 SECONDS even when the graph is fully current and nothing changed —
`--skip-flows` still runs a full import-resolution pass and reconciles embeddings. Behind a
30 s timeout it was killed on every edit AND every shell command, and nothing reported it.
Cost measured in one agent session on that repo: 152 Edit/Write calls at a mean of 29.9 s,
57% of all tool wait. Bash averaged 6.5 s INCLUDING every test run. On a 1,129-file repo the
same command is 6.2 s, which is why this went unnoticed for so long: it completes on small
repos and strangles on large ones, and the boundary moves as a repo grows.
Freshness is the watch daemon's job. SessionStart below registers the repo and starts the
daemon if it is down; the daemon then polls in the background and blocks nothing. Its watch
list lives in ~/.code-review-graph/, so it is per-user rather than per-project.
See generate_hooks_config() in code_review_graph/skills.py for the full account.

hooks.command: cat >/dev/null || true; command -v code-review-graph >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; CRG_REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; if [ -n "$CRG_REPO" ]; then code-review-graph daemon add "$CRG_REPO" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; code-review-graph daemon status 2>/dev/null | grep -qi 'daemon: *running' || { code-review-graph daemon start >/dev/null 2>&1 & }; code-review-graph status --repo "$CRG_REPO" || true; else echo 'Not a git repo, skipping'; fi
